copy.headline: Study finds North Texas could see billions in flood damages. Here’s what can help mitigate
copy.caption:
A White Settlement flood control project is one of many priority areas identified in regional study addressing flood risks. For years, homes and military facilities — including the Texas Army National Guard and the Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base — dealt with regular flooding along the Farmers Branch Creek.

The creek runs through White Settlement and across hilly terrain that once caused rain water to flow down to homes in several neighborhoods — leading to millions in damage.

story.summary: A White Settlement flood control project is one of many priority areas identified in regional study addressing flood risks. For years, homes and military facilities — including the Texas Army National Guard and the Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base — dealt with regular flooding along the Farmers Branch Creek. The creek runs through White Settlement and across hilly terrain that once caused rain water to flow down to homes in several neighborhoods — leading to millions in damage. But in the summer, officials with the North Central Texas Council of Governments, White Settlement and the Texas Military Department gathered to celebrate the completion of a $1.8 million flood control project following two years of construction.
